title: Exclusive | Inside the Scramble to Avert Conflict With Russia in the Baltic
html:
When two Nordic leaders called Russian President Vladimir Putin last month, their official order of business was to discuss ending the war in Ukraine.

But Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre had another urgent mission: preventing a clash with Russia in their own backyard, said people familiar with the matter.

The Baltic Sea had become one of the world’s most dangerous potential flashpoints between Moscow and the West, and the two leaders wanted to ease tensions by reassuring Putin they had no intention of cutting off a vital shipping route for Moscow.

Russia ships more than 60% of its seaborne oil through the Baltic Sea, providing a lifeline for its wartime economy. But the sea is surrounded by North Atlantic Treaty Organization members. The potential for conflict was highlighted in recent days by a Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian cargo ship near Finland. Coordination between Finnish and Russian authorities to rescue and recover the ship helped prevent the situation from escalating.

summary: Two Nordic leaders, with the help of an oligarch, sought out a direct line to Vladimir Putin to ease fears about a NATO blockade of the crucial waterway.
